summary: @7nohe/openapi-react-query-codegen 3.0.4 executes an obfuscated dropper on npm install
details: Version 3.0.4 of this OpenAPI/React Query codegen package ships an undeclared, obfuscated payload at the tarball root (3FWCvzduYZg.js, ~6.4 MB) that is auto-executed at install time through two independent triggers. package.json declares "preinstall": "node 3FWCvzduYZg.js", and 3FWCvzduYZg.js XOR-decodes a large char-code array with key 229 and passes the decoded string to Function() for immediate evaluation. The tarball's binding.gyp adds a second, hidden trigger: its conditions field uses a Python subclass-traversal sandbox-escape idiom (().__class__.__base__.__subclasses__() -> catch_warnings -> __builtins__['__import__']('os').system(...)) with unicode-escaped identifiers to shell out to `node 3FWCvzduYZg.js` during node-gyp configure, so the dropper still runs even if lifecycle scripts are disabled. The binding.gyp references a native source file (dog.c) that is not present in the tarball, so there is no legitimate native build. The file 3FWCvzduYZg.js is also outside the package.json "files" whitelist (which declares only "dist"), consistent with a smuggled payload rather than a build artifact. There is no legitimate reason for a codegen library to ship or execute an obfuscated preinstall payload; installing this version runs attacker-controlled code on the developer or build host.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
